name: Battle of Jutland
note: The plan shows the whole operation of 31 May and 1 June 1916 at the scale of fleets, not a single field. The accounts give distances and compass bearings only roughly, so the squadrons are placed to match them and the plan is not to scale. The accounts do not say where the British battlecruisers stood during the night, so they are left off the last phase.

terrain.name: Jutland
terrain.quote: off the North Sea coast of Denmark's Jutland Peninsula

terrain.name: Horns Reef
terrain.quote: Scheer opted to cross Jellicoe's wake and escape via Horns Reef.

sides.name: Imperial German Navy, High Seas Fleet

units.name: Grand Fleet battleships
units.quote: deploy his battleships from their cruising formation (six columns of four ships each)

units.name: 3rd Battlecruiser Squadron
units.quote: Jellicoe had ordered Rear-Admiral Horace Hood's 3rd Battlecruiser Squadron to speed ahead to find and support Beatty's force

units.name: Beatty's battlecruisers
units.quote: Beatty's ships were divided into three columns, with the two battlecruiser squadrons leading in parallel lines

units.name: 5th Battle Squadron
units.quote: The 5th Battle Squadron was stationed 5 mi (4.3 nmi; 8.0 km) to the north-west

units.name: Grand Fleet rear screen
units.quote: He placed a screen of cruisers and destroyers 5 mi (4.3 nmi; 8.0 km) behind his battle fleet

units.name: HMS Defence
units.quote: Arbuthnot's flagship, the armoured cruiser HMS Defence

units.name: German battlecruisers
units.quote: The battlecruisers were in line ahead, with the four cruisers of the II scouting group plus supporting torpedo boats ranged in an arc

units.name: German scouting cruisers
units.quote: Heavily outnumbered by Boedicker's four light cruisers

units.name: High Seas Fleet battle line
units.quote: The High Seas Fleet similarly adopted a line-ahead formation, with close screening by torpedo boats to either side

phases.title: The fleets sail towards each other unseen
phases.text: Beatty's ships ran east while Hipper's battlecruisers ran north, with Scheer's battle line following Hipper. Jellicoe's fleet was still out of sight to the north-west, and the Germans did not know it was at sea.
phases.quote: By around 14:00, Beatty's ships were proceeding eastward at roughly the same latitude as Hipper's squadron, which was heading north.

phases.title: The Run to the South
phases.text: Hipper turned south-east to lead Beatty towards Scheer and opened fire with the British to the south-west of him. The British battlecruisers followed. The German ships scored hits on three of the six British battlecruisers before the British scored their first.
phases.quote: At 15:48, with the opposing forces roughly parallel at 15,000 yd (14,000 m), with the British to the south-west of the Germans (i.e., on the right side), Hipper opened fire

phases.title: The 5th Battle Squadron comes into range
phases.text: Barham, leading the 5th Battle Squadron, caught up with Hipper at 16:08 and opened fire, and by 16:15 all four battleships were engaged. Hipper now faced them astern as well as Beatty's battlecruisers. Hood's squadron had been sent ahead from Jellicoe at about 16:05.
phases.quote: At 16:08, the lead battleship of the 5th Battle Squadron, HMS Barham, caught up with Hipper and opened fire at extreme range

phases.title: Beatty turns north and the Germans follow
phases.text: Beatty sighted the vanguard of Scheer's battle line and turned his battlecruisers through 180° to draw the Germans towards Jellicoe. The 5th Battle Squadron, too far behind to read his flags, passed them on an opposing course, heading for the German main body.
phases.quote: Beatty turned his battlecruiser force 180°, heading north to draw the Germans toward Jellicoe.

phases.title: The 5th Battle Squadron acts as rearguard
phases.text: Scheer's leading battleships opened fire at 16:48. The 5th Battle Squadron turned north and drew fire from Hipper's battlecruisers and Scheer's leading battleships, while Beatty eased his own ships out of range by 17:10.
phases.quote: For the next hour, the 5th Battle Squadron acted as Beatty's rearguard, drawing fire from all the German ships within range

phases.title: Hood meets the German scouting ships
phases.text: Hood's battlecruisers came up and relieved the scout cruiser Chester, which had been pounded by Boedicker's four light cruisers. They disabled the light cruiser Wiesbaden, and Boedicker's other ships turned towards Hipper and Scheer.
phases.quote: Heavily outnumbered by Boedicker's four light cruisers, Chester was pounded before being relieved by Hood's heavy units

phases.title: Jellicoe deploys to the east
phases.text: Hipper turned back towards Scheer at about 18:00, and Boedicker's ships fell back on him. Jellicoe, needing to turn his six columns into a single battle line, ordered deployment to the east at 18:15; it would take twenty minutes.
phases.quote: In one of the most critical and difficult tactical command decisions of the entire war, Jellicoe ordered deployment to the east at 18:15.

phases.title: Windy Corner: Defence is lost
phases.text: Beatty's battlecruisers crossed the front of the British battleships to join Hood. Arbuthnot's flagship Defence charged across his bows and ran into the guns of Hipper's and Scheer's oncoming ships, which blew her up with all hands.
phases.quote: Arbuthnot's flagship, the armoured cruiser HMS Defence, and her squadron-mate HMS Warrior both charged across Beatty's bows

phases.title: Invincible blows up and Lützow is crippled
phases.text: Hipper came within range of Hood's squadron and Beatty's ships, and the German flagship Lützow was hit many times. At 18:30 Invincible appeared as a clear target and was sunk in 90 seconds by Lützow and Derfflinger; Hood was killed.
phases.quote: But at 18:30, Invincible abruptly appeared as a clear target before Lützow and Derfflinger.

phases.title: Scheer's T is crossed and he turns away
phases.text: The leading German battleships came out of the mist facing the whole British line, which crossed their T. Scheer ordered a turn together through 180°, and the German fleet disengaged under smoke and mist.
phases.quote: Realising he was heading into a death trap, Scheer ordered his fleet to turn and disengage at 18:33.

phases.title: Scheer doubles back to the east
phases.text: Jellicoe did not chase directly but headed south, keeping the High Seas Fleet west of him. Scheer, judging it not yet dark enough to escape, doubled back to the east, which took his ships again towards Jellicoe's deployed line.
phases.quote: Scheer, knowing that it was not yet dark enough to escape and that his fleet would suffer terribly in a stern chase, doubled back to the east at 18:55.

phases.title: The T is crossed again and the battlecruisers charge
phases.text: By 19:15 Jellicoe had crossed Scheer's T again. Scheer turned west a second time and sent his torpedo boats and the four remaining battlecruisers of Hipper's group at the British to cover the turn, under heavy fire.
phases.quote: Scheer ordered a major torpedo attack by his destroyers and a potentially sacrificial charge by Scouting Group I's four remaining battlecruisers.

phases.title: The last exchanges after sunset
phases.text: Just after sunset the surviving British battlecruisers caught up with the German battlecruisers, which were briefly relieved by the older pre-dreadnoughts. These were the last major exchanges between capital ships in the battle and in the war.
phases.quote: as the surviving British battlecruisers caught up with their German counterparts

phases.title: Scheer slips round the British rear in the night
phases.text: Jellicoe headed south with a screen of cruisers and destroyers behind him to guard Scheer's expected escape route. Scheer instead crossed the British wake and made for Horns Reef, passing through the screen.
phases.quote: In reality, Scheer opted to cross Jellicoe's wake and escape via Horns Reef.
